title: PointNet++: Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space
layout_note: A shared hierarchy on the left (five point-set planes in a light-grey panel) splits through two hollow block arrows into two heads stacked on the right: Segmentation on top (five planes going back up the hierarchy) and Classification below (one plane, a vector bar, a node-link fully connected net, a score bar). Two dotted elbow lines leave planes inside the left panel, run above everything along the top edge and drop with arrowheads onto two segmentation planes.
grouping: The hierarchy sits in one light-grey rectangular panel with a soft drop shadow, titled in bold italic serif just above it; the two heads have no container, only bold-italic serif headings of the same style ('Segmentation', 'Classification'). Inside the panel, curly braces under each pair of steps group 'sampling & grouping' + 'pointnet' as one 'set abstraction'. Plane colour marks hierarchy level: two green planes for the full-resolution set, two blue for the first level, red for the second; the segmentation head repeats these colours in reverse (red, blue, blue, green, green).
shapes_depth: Point sets are flat sheared parallelograms with no thickness or outline, filled in solid green, blue or red and set at the same slant so they read as sheets seen in perspective; points are small dots on them (grey on green, dark blue on blue, pale yellow ovals on red). Grouping is drawn as dashed circles on a plane, with dotted lines converging from each circle to its single point on the next plane; interpolation is drawn as short solid black lines converging from several points to one, plus thin dotted horizontals between planes. Tensor sizes are rotated serif labels along each plane's top edge. Short black filled-head arrows with serif labels sit under the gaps between planes. The classification head uses plain grey vertical bars for vectors and a node-link net of hollow circles in three columns with dense thin edges. The branch arrows are wide hollow outlined block arrows.
proposed_highlight: The method's own repeated unit is named by curly braces labelled 'set abstraction' under each sampling-and-grouping plus pointnet pair, and the whole hierarchy is set apart in a grey shadowed panel with its own bold-italic title; the two applications are only given matching bold-italic headings. There is no legend and no coloured module box: the steps are named by plain serif text under arrows.
lesson: Each hierarchy level keeps one plane colour (green, blue, red) and the segmentation head reuses them in reverse, so the dotted skip lines running over the top of the figure visibly join planes of the same colour.
notes: Venue NeurIPS 2017 from semantic-scholar (venue and venue year verified). The point-set planes are perspective sheets rather than stacked feature-map blocks, recorded as element 'other'. `refs crop` recorded the whole grey left panel (plus several thin slivers along plane edges) as embedded raster images, so photo_share measures that panel rather than photographs, and the measured palette describes mainly the right-hand heads and the area outside the panel.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: set abstraction drawn on the point set itself: a row of tilted planes dotted with points, where dashed grouping balls on one plane are traced by dotted funnel lines to single centroid points on the next, the plane colour changing per resolution level (green -> blue -> red)

relations.form: inside a grey left panel five tilted planes run left to right, joined by short arrows labeled 'sampling & grouping' and 'pointnet', with (N,d+C)-style shapes above each plane
two curly braces under the panel group the planes into two repeated 'set abstraction' levels with identical internal steps
two hollow arrows branch from the panel into a 'Segmentation' row on top and a 'Classification' row below, both starting from the red coarsest plane

the segmentation row climbs back up the levels (red -> blue -> blue -> green -> green per-point scores) via 'interpolate' and 'unit pointnet', with solid lines from coarse points fanning into finer points
two dotted skip lines run over the top of the figure from backbone planes down into the matching segmentation planes
the classification row pools the red plane with a pointnet into a grey (1,C4) bar, then a node-link fully connected network, then a grey class-score bar

channels.colour: plane colour = resolution level (green full, blue first abstraction, red second), reused in the segmentation decoder so matching levels pair up; grey = pooled vectors (global feature, class scores) and also the backbone panel background
channels.shape: tilted planes = point sets at one resolution, dots = points, dashed ellipses/circles = grouping regions, node-link graph = fully connected layers, grey bars = vectors
channels.line: short black arrows = operation steps; dotted lines = grouping funnels and skip links; solid lines between points = interpolation; hollow block arrows = branching into the two task heads
channels.frame: a grey panel = the shared backbone; braces = one set-abstraction unit; the heads are unframed

quality.strengths: the hierarchical grouping is shown on the data - grouping balls and funnels from regions to centroids across planes - so 'local regions become points' reads without text; colour encodes resolution level and is reused in the decoder; the two set abstraction levels are drawn identically and braced as one unit
quality.weaknesses: the dotted skip links run over the top of the whole figure, long and easy to miss, with a near-dead dotted spur entering the backbone title; grey carries both 'vector' and 'backbone panel'; the classification head's generic node-link MLP takes about as much space as the novel set abstraction steps

insights.structure: A grey panel on the left titled 'Hierarchical point set feature learning' holds two 'set abstraction' levels (braced underneath); two hollow arrows branch right into a 'Segmentation' row on top and a 'Classification' row below.
insights.data: Point sets are tilted colored planes (green, blue, red per level) dotted with points, grouping balls are dashed ellipses, shapes (N,d+C) sit on each plane, and the classifier uses a fully-connected node-link network ending in a grey score bar.
insights.emphasis: Plane color changes per abstraction level and is reused in the segmentation decoder, so matching-resolution levels pair up across the backbone and head.
insights.flow: Left to right with small black arrows labeled by the op (sampling & grouping, pointnet, interpolate, unit pointnet); dotted skip lines run over the top from backbone levels to the segmentation decoder.
insights.avoid: Skip-link dotted lines run along the very top edge across the panel boundary and are faint, so which level connects to which is hard to trace.

arrangement.units: a grey-filled backbone panel on the left, then two unframed task heads (Segmentation above, Classification below) titled in bold italic
arrangement.shared: backbone output feeds both heads via two hollow arrows
